results.text: The metals and minerals index is projected to edge 3 percent (y/y) lower in 2027 as supply conditions improve somewhat for several base metals owing to fading production or export disruptions and new capacity coming on stream. For copper, however, mined supply growth is anticipated to remain subdued, reflecting factors such as declining ore grades in Chile, the world’s largest producer. Assuming global economic growth holds up, buoyant base metal demand driven by, for example, the expansion of renewable energy infrastructure, electric vehicles, and data centers is likely to keep medium-term prices elevated (figure 4.F). Precious metal prices are also expected to register a steep average increase of 40 percent in 2026, amid strong demand for diversifying financial assets against a strained geopolitical backdrop. Gold and silver are both in line to set annual price records.

Metal prices are forecast to inch down in 2027, but a high-price regime is expected to remain entrenched, with the metals and minerals price index projected to exceed its 2021 peak by 16 percent. Demand for base metals is anticipated to hold firm, underpinned by robust investment in electrification infrastructure, renewable energy, and data centers, which are base-metal-intensive. However, subdued conventional construction in many economies and weakness in China’s steel sector are likely to weigh on iron ore prices. The precious metals price index fell by 7 percent in 2026Q3 after reaching all-time highs earlier in the year. Still, the index is on track to increase by 40 percent in 2026, before drifting lower by 8 percent in 2027 as investor demand moderates.

Over the five years through 2030, the World Bank Group is targeting a fivefold increase in financing of the metals and minerals sector, to $19 billion, to support mineral-rich EMDEs in converting their natural endowments into lasting prosperity. T o foster dynamic private sectors and help create jobs more broadly, the World Bank Group has accelerated and simplified its ability to catalyze private capital flows alongside its financing and knowledge services. Through enhanced private capital mobilization, the institution will seek to deepen investment in the next generation of youth in client countries—in particular, by improving the conditions for job creation.

results.text: FERTILIZERSCOMMODITY MARKETS OUTLOOK | OCTOBER 2026 39 Recent developments Nitrogen (urea) prices averaged $399/mt in 2026Q3, down 42 percent (q/q) and 18 percent (y/y), after peaking at $857/mt in April (figure 18.A). Prices eased further in the first half of October. The initial retreat during 2026Q2 reflected China’s easing of export restrictions in May, the temporary reduction in hostilities following the June memorandum of understand- ing between the United States and the Islamic Republic of Iran, and reductions in purchases, partly owing to the end of spring planting in the Northern Hemisphere. Increased exports from China and other major suppliers, including Egypt, Nigeria, and Oman, helped sustain a return to more normal price levels. China’s urea exports are expected to reach 7.0 million metric tons (mmt) in 2026, up from 4.9 mmt in 2025.

Urea prices are forecast to fall by 16 percent in 2027 and 14 percent in 2028, assuming Middle Eastern exports recover, natural gas prices ease, Fertilizers The World Bank Group’s fertilizer price index fell by 22 percent in 2026Q3 (q/q) and continued to decline in October, fully reversing the 2026Q2 surge that followed the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Urea prices drove both swings, while other fertilizer prices rose less sharply but remained elevated in 2026Q3. Despite the recent retreat, the index is projected to rise by about 14 percent in 2026 (y/y), reflecting shipping disruptions in the Middle East, associated increases in input costs, and trade restrictions. Prices are forecast to fall by 12 percent in 2027 and a further 8 percent in 2028 as input costs ease and supplies recover, aided by increased exports from producers outside the Gulf region.

Upside risks to the outlook for urea prices include an escalation in the Middle East conflict that raises input costs, particularly for natural gas, above baseline expectations. More specifically, continued conflict could lead to an extension of Qatar’s force majeure, imposed in March, on contracts to sell LNG and related products, including urea. Export restrictions by major producers are another potential source of renewed price surges. Conversely, a swift reduction of geopolitical tensions in the Gulf region could lead to a surge of exports, materially lowering prices, although infrastructure damage is likely to delay the full recovery of urea production. After a projected 7 percent increase in 2026, DAP prices are forecast to drop by about 18 percent in 2027 and 17 percent in 2028.

SPECIAL FOCUS COMMODITY MARKETS OUTLOOK | OCTOBER 2026 48 Introduction Commodity prices often move in tandem because many markets are exposed to common shifts in global activity, input costs, trade, and financial conditions. For instance, a slowdown in industrial activity can weaken demand for energy and industrial metals at the same time, while disruptions to energy supply can raise transport and fertilizer costs and spill into agricultural markets. Periods of financial or geopolitical stress can broaden these movements across otherwise distinct commodity groups (World Bank 2024). Understanding these linkages is key because commodity price shocks affect inflation, fiscal revenues, trade balances, and food and energy security, particularly in emerging market and developing economies (EMDEs) with large commodity exposures (Balcilar, Usman and Agan 2024; World Bank 2026a).

Most commodity analysis appropriately focuses on the supply and demand fundamentals of individual markets. While that approach remains important, it provides only a partial view when volatility associated with one commodity is linked to developments in other commodity markets. This Special Focus examines price volatility connectedness across 15 internationally traded commodities in six groups—energy, food, industrial metals, livestock, precious metals, and soft commodities (such as coffee and cotton)— using daily data from 2006 to 2026. Price volatility connectedness measures how much of the variance in a commodity’s price volatility can be explained by shocks affecting prices in other commodity markets.

The main risks to the baseline forecast are related to weather, particularly El Niño, which has historically reduced cocoa yields through drier-than-normal conditions, especially in the rainfed production areas of Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana. T ea prices are expected to increase by 4 percent in 2027 and by 2 percent in 2028 as demand recovers, particularly in the Middle East.

Average beverage prices are forecast to broadly stabilize thereafter, as declining coffee prices partly offset a pickup in cocoa prices. In all, the World Bank Group’s agricultural commodity price index—a composite measure for food, beverages, and raw materials—is forecast to inch up this year, then gain 5 percent in 2027. The effects of El Niño are evident in several price forecast revisions relative to April 2026. The palm oil price forecast, for instance, has been revised higher by 15 percent in 2027 amid unusually dry conditions in Indonesia.
